critical_code_review_comments: couchbase_db.py find_one_and_update implementation is correct: KV fast-path for id-only filters (single round trip get + replace), N1QL fallback for general filters, supports return_document (BEFORE/AFTER), upsert, and projection. Mirrors Motor semantics adequately for what the app uses.
find_one_and_delete is similarly correct (KV fast-path + N1QL fallback) and returns the removed doc snapshot.

Note: ReturnDocument enum from pymongo is NOT explicitly supported — code does `bool(return_document)` which works because ReturnDocument.AFTER == True and ReturnDocument.BEFORE == False in pymongo, but if someone passes a non-bool truthy value it could surprise. Low risk since callers in this repo pass `return_document=True` literally.

Minor: the upsert branch in the GENERAL find_one_and_update path returns None when not return_after even after creating a new doc; Motor would arguably return None too because there is no BEFORE — that matches but is worth a code comment.

Audit was clean: the only callers of find_one_and_update / find_one_and_delete in /app/backend/routes are users.update_user and reservations.confirm_reservation / confirm_reservation_with_photo — all three now pass the Couchbase adapter.
